schema: CREATE CONSTRAINT jurisdiction_code IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Jurisdiction) REQUIRE n.code IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT sector_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Sector) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT regulator_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Regulator) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT tx_typology_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:TxTypology) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT guidance_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Guidance) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT instrument_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Instrument) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT law_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Law) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT article_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Article) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT source_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Source) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT entity_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Entity) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT sanctions_list_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:SanctionsList) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT address_key IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Address) REQUIRE n.key IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT proposal_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Proposal) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT risk_category_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:RiskCategory) REQUIRE n.id IS UNIQUE
CREATE CONSTRAINT source_kind IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Source) REQUIRE n.kind IS NOT NULL
CREATE CONSTRAINT source_url IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Source) REQUIRE n.url IS NOT NULL
CREATE CONSTRAINT source_date IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Source) REQUIRE n.date IS NOT NULL
CREATE CONSTRAINT source_amount_type IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Source) REQUIRE n.amount :: FLOAT
CREATE CONSTRAINT source_verify_type IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Source) REQUIRE n.verify :: BOOLEAN
CREATE CONSTRAINT jurisdiction_wave_type IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Jurisdiction) REQUIRE n.wave :: INTEGER
CREATE CONSTRAINT proposal_status IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Proposal) REQUIRE n.status IS NOT NULL
CREATE INDEX source_date_idx IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Source) ON (n.date)
CREATE INDEX regulator_short_idx IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Regulator) ON (n.short)
CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX crypto_case_text IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Source) ON EACH [n.title, n.summary, n.chain, n.party]
load:
UNWIND $j AS j
MERGE (x:Jurisdiction {code: j.code}) SET x.name = j.name, x.wave = j.wave, x.regime = j.regime, x.travel_rule = j.travel_rule, x.verify = j.verify
MERGE (s:Sector {id: j.sector}) SET s.name = 'crypto-asset service providers', s.group = 'crypto'
MERGE (s)-[:IN_JURISDICTION]->(x)

UNWIND $j AS j UNWIND j.regulators AS r
MATCH (s:Sector {id: j.sector})
MERGE (g:Regulator {id: r.id}) SET g.short = r.short, g.name = r.name, g.url = r.url
MERGE (g)-[v:SUPERVISES]->(s) SET v.role = r.role, v.aml = r.aml

UNWIND $j AS j UNWIND j.laws AS l
MATCH (s:Sector {id: j.sector})
MERGE (w:Law {id: l.id}) SET w.short = l.short, w.title = l.title, w.url = l.url
MERGE (s)-[:SUBJECT_TO]->(w)

UNWIND $c AS c
MERGE (k:Source {id: c.id}) SET k.kind = 'case', k.title = c.title, k.party = c.party, k.date = c.date, k.measure = c.measure,
  k.amount = CASE WHEN c.amount IS NULL THEN null ELSE toFloat(c.amount) END, k.currency = c.currency, k.amount_note = c.amount_note,
  k.summary = c.summary, k.chain = c.chain, k.url = c.url, k.verify = c.verify,
  k.published = c.published, k.status = c.status, k.period = c.period, k.decision = c.decision, k.note = c.note, k.violated_from = c.violated_from
MERGE (e:Entity {id: 'ENTITY:' + coalesce(c.group, toLower(c.party))}) SET e.name = coalesce(e.name, c.party), e.group = c.group
MERGE (k)-[:AGAINST]->(e)
WITH k, c MATCH (x:Jurisdiction {code: c.jurisdiction}) MERGE (k)-[:IN_JURISDICTION]->(x)

UNWIND $c AS c UNWIND c.authorities AS a
MATCH (k:Source {id: c.id})
MATCH (x:Jurisdiction {code: c.jurisdiction})<-[:IN_JURISDICTION]-(:Sector)<-[:SUPERVISES]-(g:Regulator {short: a})
MERGE (k)-[:BY]->(g)

UNWIND $c AS c UNWIND c.violated AS v
MATCH (k:Source {id: c.id}) MATCH (w:Law {id: v.law})
MERGE (k)-[r:VIOLATED {art: coalesce(v.art, '')}]->(w) SET r.lids = coalesce(v.lids, []), r.stated = coalesce(v.stated, false)

UNWIND [c IN $c WHERE c.power IS NOT NULL] AS c
MATCH (k:Source {id: c.id}) MATCH (w:Law {id: c.power.law})
MERGE (k)-[r:UNDER_POWER {art: c.power.art}]->(w) SET r.point = c.power.point

UNWIND $a AS a
MATCH (w:Law {id: a.law})
MERGE (x:Article {id: a.law + ':' + a.art}) SET x.law = a.law, x.law_short = w.short, x.art = a.art, x.heading = a.heading, x.duty = a.duty,
  x.text = a.text, x.status = a.status, x.version = a.version, x.source_sha256 = a.sha256
MERGE (w)-[:HAS_ARTICLE]->(x)

UNWIND $a AS a UNWIND a.replaced_by AS r
MATCH (x:Article {id: a.law + ':' + a.art}) MATCH (y:Article {id: r})
MERGE (x)-[:REPLACED_BY]->(y)

UNWIND $c AS c UNWIND c.violated AS v
MATCH (k:Source {id: c.id}) MATCH (x:Article {id: v.law + ':' + coalesce(v.art, '')})
MERGE (k)-[r:VIOLATED_ARTICLE]->(x) SET r.lids = coalesce(v.lids, []), r.stated = coalesce(v.stated, false)

UNWIND $l AS l
MERGE (x:SanctionsList {id: l.id}) SET x.name = l.name, x.url = l.url, x.refresh = l.refresh, x.imported = coalesce(l.imported, false),
  x.entries_total = l.entries_total, x.addresses_total = l.addresses_total, x.fetched = l.fetched, x.sha256 = l.sha256
WITH x, l OPTIONAL MATCH (g:Regulator {id: l.owner}) FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN g IS NULL THEN [] ELSE [1] END | MERGE (x)-[:PUBLISHED_BY]->(g))

UNWIND $s AS e
MATCH (l:SanctionsList {id: e.list})
MERGE (x:Entity {id: e.id}) SET x.name = e.name, x.type = e.type, x.programs = e.programs, x.aliases = e.aliases, x.listed = true
MERGE (l)-[:LISTS]->(x)
WITH x, l, e UNWIND e.addresses AS a
MERGE (y:Address {key: a.chain + ':' + a.address}) SET y.chain = a.chain, y.address = a.address, y.currency = a.currency, y.unlabelled = coalesce(a.unlabelled, false)
MERGE (x)-[:CONTROLS]->(y)
MERGE (l)-[:LISTS]->(y)

UNWIND $t AS t
MERGE (a:Address {key: t.from_key}) ON CREATE SET a.chain = t.chain, a.address = t.from
MERGE (b:Address {key: t.to_key}) ON CREATE SET b.chain = t.chain, b.address = t.to
MERGE (a)-[f:SENT {asset: t.asset}]->(b) SET f.amount = t.amount, f.count = t.count, f.first = t.first, f.last = t.last, f.tx = t.tx, f.hop = t.hop

UNWIND $ts AS x
MATCH (a:Address {key: x.key}) SET a.traced = x.fetched, a.hop = x.hop, a.balance = x.balance, a.balance_asset = x.asset, a.received = x.received, a.sent = x.sent, a.tx_count = x.tx_count

UNWIND $rc AS c
MERGE (x:RiskCategory {id: c.id}) SET x.name = c.name, x.severity = c.severity, x.group = c.group, x.description = c.description

UNWIND $ec AS m
MATCH (e:Entity {id: m.entity}) MATCH (x:RiskCategory {id: m.category})
MERGE (e)-[r:IN_CATEGORY]->(x) SET r.by = m.by

UNWIND $c AS c UNWIND coalesce(c.typologies, []) AS t
MATCH (k:Source {id: c.id}) MATCH (x:RiskCategory {id: t})
MERGE (k)-[:TYPOLOGY]->(x)

UNWIND $al AS x
MERGE (a:Address {key: x.key}) SET a.label = x.label, a.label_source = x.source, a.label_scam = x.is_scam
WITH a, x WHERE x.category IS NOT NULL
MATCH (c:RiskCategory {id: x.category})
MERGE (a)-[r:IN_CATEGORY]->(c) SET r.by = 'label: ' + x.label

UNWIND $m AS m
MATCH (a:Entity {id: m.case_entity}) MATCH (b:Entity {id: m.listed})
MERGE (a)-[r:POSSIBLY_SAME]->(b) SET r.by = m.by
UNWIND $tt AS x MERGE (t:TxTypology {id: x.id}) SET t.name = x.name, t.severity = x.severity, t.level = x.level, t.rule = x.rule

UNWIND $gd AS x MERGE (g:Guidance {id: x.id}) SET g.title = x.title, g.issuer = x.issuer_name, g.date = x.date, g.url = x.url, g.kind = x.kind, g.status = x.status, g.summary = x.summary, g.verify = x.verify, g.applies_from = x.applies_from
UNWIND $gd AS x MATCH (g:Guidance {id: x.id}) MATCH (r:Regulator {id: x.issuer}) MERGE (r)-[:ISSUED]->(g)
UNWIND $tg AS x MATCH (t:TxTypology {id: x.typology}) MATCH (g:Guidance {id: x.guidance}) MERGE (t)-[r:FLAGGED_IN {section: x.section}]->(g) SET r.page = x.page, r.says = x.says

UNWIND $tl AS x MATCH (a:Address {key: x.key}) MATCH (t:TxTypology {id: x.typology}) MERGE (a)-[r:SHOWS {asset: x.asset}]->(t) SET r.evidence = x.evidence, r.n = x.n, r.first = x.first, r.last = x.last
UNWIND $te AS x MATCH (a:Address {key: x.from_key})-[s:SENT {asset: x.asset}]->(b:Address {key: x.to_key}) SET s.typologies = x.typologies

UNWIND $in AS x MERGE (i:Instrument {id: x.id}) SET i.symbol = x.symbol, i.name = x.name, i.chain = x.chain, i.model = x.model, i.standard = x.standard, i.kind = x.kind, i.issuer = x.issuer, i.contract = x.contract, i.freeze = x.freeze, i.traceable = x.traceable, i.risk = x.risk, i.sanctioned = x.sanctioned_what, i.sanctioned_from = x.sanctioned_from, i.sanctioned_by = x.sanctioned_by, i.sanction_source = x.sanctioned_source, i.verify = coalesce(x.verify, false)
UNWIND $in AS x UNWIND x.guidance AS gid MATCH (i:Instrument {id: x.id}) MATCH (g:Guidance {id: gid}) MERGE (i)-[:ADDRESSED_IN]->(g)

a.heading: Vergunningverlening
a.duty: no crypto-asset services in the Union without authorisation as a CASP (or a notification under art. 60)
a.text: Vergunningverlening 1. Een persoon mag binnen de Unie geen cryptoactivadiensten aanbieden, tenzij die persoon: a. een rechtspersoon of andere onderneming is die overeenkomstig artikel 63 een vergunning als aanbieder van crypto­ activadiensten heeft gekregen, of b. een kredietinstelling, een centrale effectenbewaarinstelling, een beleggingsonderneming, een marktexploitant, een instelling voor elektronisch geld, een icbe-beheermaatschappij of een abi-beheerder die overeenkomstig artikel 60 cryptoactivadiensten mag aanbieden. 9.6.2023 2. Aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten die overeenkomstig artikel 63 een vergunning hebben gekregen, hebben een statutaire zetel in een lidstaat waar zij ten minste een deel van hun cryptoactivadiensten verrichten. Zij hebben hun plaats van werkelijke leiding in de Unie en ten minste één van de directeuren is woonachtig in de Unie. 3. Voor de toepassing van lid 1, punt a), mogen andere ondernemingen die geen rechtspersoon zijn alleen crypto­ activadiensten aanbieden indien hun rechtsvorm een niveau van bescherming van de belangen van derden waarborgt dat gelijkwaardig is aan het door rechtspersonen geboden beschermingsniveau en indien zij onderworpen zijn aan een gelijkwaardig prudentieel toezicht dat aan hun rechtsvorm is aangepast. 4. Aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten die overeenkomstig artikel 63 een vergunning hebben gekregen, voldoen te allen tijde aan de voorwaarden voor hun vergunning. 5. Een persoon die geen aanbieder van cryptoactivadien

a.heading: Aanbieding van cryptoactivadiensten door bepaalde financiële entiteiten
a.duty: credit institutions and other financial entities may offer crypto-asset services after a notification
a.text: Aanbieding van cryptoactivadiensten door bepaalde financiële entiteiten 1. Een kredietinstelling mag cryptoactivadiensten aanbieden indien zij de bevoegde autoriteit van haar lidstaat van herkomst ten minste 40 werkdagen voordat zij die diensten voor het eerst aanbiedt in kennis stelt van de in lid 7 bedoelde informatie. 2. Een centrale effectenbewaarinstelling die op grond van Verordening (EU) nr. 909/2014 van het Europees Parlement en de Raad (45) een vergunning heeft gekregen, mag slechts cryptoactiva namens cliënten bewaren en beheren indien zij de bevoegde autoriteit van de lidstaat van herkomst ten minste 40 werkdagen voordat zij die dienst voor het eerst aanbiedt in kennis stelt van de in lid 7 van dit artikel bedoelde informatie. Voor de toepassing van de eerste alinea van dit lid wordt het bewaren en beheren van cryptoactiva namens cliënten geacht gelijkwaardig te zijn aan het aanbieden, aanhouden of exploiteren van effectenrekeningen in verband met de afwikkelingsdienst als bedoeld in afdeling B, punt 3, van de bijlage bij Verordening (EU) nr. 909/2014. 3. Een beleggingsonderneming mag cryptoactivadiensten in de Unie aanbieden die gelijkwaardig zijn aan de beleg­ gingsdiensten en -activiteiten waarvoor zij op grond van Richtlijn 2014/65/EU over een specifieke vergunning beschikt, indien zij de bevoegde autoriteit van de lidstaat van herkomst ten minste 40 werkdagen voordat zij deze diensten voor het eerst aanbiedt, in kennis stelt van de in lid 7 van dit artikel bed

a.heading: Verlening van cryptoactivadiensten uitsluitend op initiatief van de cliënt
a.duty: reverse solicitation
a.text: Verlening van cryptoactivadiensten uitsluitend op initiatief van de cliënt 1. Indien een cliënt die in de Unie is gevestigd of gesitueerd, uitsluitend op eigen initiatief om de verrichting van een cryptoactivadienst of -activiteit door een onderneming uit een derde land verzoekt, is het vergunningsvereiste uit hoofde van artikel 59 niet van toepassing op de verrichting van die cryptoactivadienst of -activiteit door de onderneming uit een derde land voor die cliënt, noch op een betrekking die specifiek verband houdt met het verrichten van die crypto­ activadienst of -activiteit. a.text: Beoordeling van de vergunningsaanvraag en toekenning of weigering van een vergunning 1. Indien de aanvraag onvolledig is, stellen de bevoegde autoriteiten een termijn vast waarbinnen de aanvragende aanbieder van cryptoactivadiensten ontbrekende informatie moet verstrekken. 3. a.heading: Prudentiële vereisten
a.duty: prudential requirements
a.text: Prudentiële vereisten 1. a.heading: Governanceregelingen
a.duty: governance
a.text: Governanceregelingen 1. Leden van het leidinggevende orgaan van aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten hebben een voldoende goede reputatie en beschikken zowel individueel als collectief over de passende kennis, vaardigheden en ervaring om hun taken te kunnen uitvoeren. In het bijzonder mogen leden van het leidinggevende orgaan van aanbieders van crypto­ activadiensten niet veroordeeld zijn voor strafbare feiten die verband houden met het witwassen van geld, terrorisme­ financiering of voor andere strafbare feiten die hun goede reputatie zouden aantasten. Zij tonen ook aan dat zij voldoende tijd aan de daadwerkelijke uitvoering van hun taken kunnen besteden. 2. a.heading: Bewaring van cryptoactiva en geldmiddelen van cliënten
a.duty: safekeeping of clients' crypto-assets and funds
a.text: Bewaring van cryptoactiva en geldmiddelen van cliënten 1. Aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten die aan cliënten toebehorende cryptoactiva of de toegangsmiddelen tot dergelijke cryptoactiva houden, treffen adequate regelingen om de eigendomsrechten van cliënten veilig te stellen, met name in het geval van de insolventie van de aanbieder van cryptoactivadiensten, en om te voorkomen dat cryptoactiva van cliënten voor hun eigen rekening worden gebruikt. 2. Indien hun bedrijfsmodellen of de cryptoactivadiensten vereisen dat andere geldmiddelen van cliënten dan emoneytokens worden aangehouden, beschikken aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten over adequate regelingen om de eigendomsrechten van cliënten veilig te stellen en om te voorkomen dat geldmiddelen van cliënten voor hun eigen rekening worden gebruikt. 3. Uiterlijk aan het einde van de werkdag volgend op de dag waarop andere geldmiddelen van cliënten dan emoneytokens zijn ontvangen, storten aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten die geldmiddelen van cliënten bij een krediet­ instelling of een centrale bank. Aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten nemen alle noodzakelijke maatregelen om ervoor te zorgen dat bij een krediet­ instelling of een centrale bank aangehouden andere geldmiddelen van cliënten dan e-moneytokens worden aangehouden op een rekening die afzonderlijk identificeerbaar is van rekeningen die worden gebruikt om aan de aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten toebehorende geldmiddelen aan te houden. 4. a.heading: Bewaring en beheer van cryptoactiva namens cliënten
a.duty: custody and administration on behalf of clients
a.text: Bewaring en beheer van cryptoactiva namens cliënten 1. In voorkomend geval leggen aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten in dat register zo snel mogelijk alle bewegingen vast volgens de instructies van hun cliënten. a.heading: Exploitatie van een cryptoactivahandelsplatform
a.duty: operation of a trading platform
a.text: Exploitatie van een cryptoactivahandelsplatform 1. Aanbieders van cryptoactivadiensten die een cryptoactivahandelsplatform exploiteren, stellen voor de exploitatie van het handelsplatform duidelijke en transparante regels vast, handhaven deze regels en voeren deze uit. a.duty: administrative penalties and measures
a.text: Administratieve sancties en andere administratieve maatregelen 1. a.heading: Overgangsmaatregelen
a.duty: transitional measures (national transition for existing providers)
a.text: Overgangsmaatregelen 1. De artikelen 4 tot en met 15 zijn niet van toepassing op aanbiedingen aan het publiek van cryptoactiva die vóór 30 december 2024 zijn afgelopen. 2. tt.name: Transfer with a listed party
tt.rule: Sender or receiver is a wallet the sanctions lists give for a listed party.
tt.rule_template: Sender or receiver is a wallet the sanctions lists give for a listed party.

tt.name: Sanctioned instrument
tt.rule: The transfer is in an instrument that is itself under a transaction ban (for example A7A5 in the EU since 25 November 2025).
tt.rule_template: The transfer is in an instrument that is itself under a transaction ban (for example A7A5 in the EU since 25 November 2025).

tt.name: High-risk counterparty
tt.rule: Sender or receiver carries a label in a high-risk category (scam, mixer, darknet, ransomware, fraud).
tt.rule_template: Sender or receiver carries a label in a high-risk category (scam, mixer, darknet, ransomware, fraud).

tt.name: Exchange or service
tt.rule: Sender or receiver carries the label of an exchange or other service: a deposit to or withdrawal from a provider.
tt.rule_template: Sender or receiver carries the label of an exchange or other service: a deposit to or withdrawal from a provider.

tt.name: Fan-out (distribution)
tt.rule: A wallet sends one asset to at least 10 different wallets within 72 hours.
tt.rule_template: A wallet sends one asset to at least {min} different wallets within {hours} hours.

tt.name: Fan-in (aggregation)
tt.rule: A wallet receives one asset from at least 10 different wallets within 72 hours.
tt.rule_template: A wallet receives one asset from at least {min} different wallets within {hours} hours.

tt.name: Pass-through (rapid in and out)
tt.rule: Within 24 hours of receiving an amount, a wallet sends on at least 0.8 of it in the same asset.
tt.rule_template: Within {hours} hours of receiving an amount, a wallet sends on at least {ratio} of it in the same asset.

tt.name: Structuring below a threshold
tt.rule: At least 3 stablecoin transfers between the same two wallets within 7 days, each between 0.85 and 100% of a threshold ([1000, 10000]); USD stablecoins compared with EUR thresholds one to one, as an approximation.
tt.rule_template: At least {count} stablecoin transfers between the same two wallets within {days} days, each between {band} and 100% of a threshold ({thresholds}); USD stablecoins compared with EUR thresholds one to one, as an approximation.

tt.name: Peeling chain
tt.rule: Bitcoin: at least 3 transactions in a row where a wallet sends most (0.75 or more) on to one new wallet and a small part elsewhere.
tt.rule_template: Bitcoin: at least {hops} transactions in a row where a wallet sends most ({share} or more) on to one new wallet and a small part elsewhere.

tt.name: Asset change (swap)
tt.rule: A wallet receives one asset and sends another within 7 days (for example USDT in, ETH out).
tt.rule_template: A wallet receives one asset and sends another within {days} days (for example USDT in, ETH out).

tt.name: Round trip
tt.rule: Money in one asset returns to the wallet it left within 3 hops.
tt.rule_template: Money in one asset returns to the wallet it left within {hops} hops.

tt.name: Large stablecoin transfer
tt.rule: One stablecoin transfer of at least 100000 (USDT, USDC).
tt.rule_template: One stablecoin transfer of at least {usd} (USDT, USDC).

tt.name: Lookalike or spam tokens received
tt.rule: A wallet receives tokens that imitate a known asset or carry advertising in their name (address poisoning, scam tokens); at least 3 such transfers.
tt.rule_template: A wallet receives tokens that imitate a known asset or carry advertising in their name (address poisoning, scam tokens); at least {min} such transfers.

tg.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions
tg.says: Transfers split into small amounts or kept below reporting thresholds.

tg.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions
tg.says: Virtual assets deposited and withdrawn again at once, without further activity.

tg.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions
tg.says: Virtual assets sent on at once to several wallets or providers, especially in places with little relation to the customer.

tg.section: Red flag indicators related to transaction patterns
tg.says: Many small amounts collected from unrelated wallets, then moved on or cashed out.

tg.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions; transaction patterns
tg.says: Conversion between virtual assets, at a loss or with extra fees, without a business rationale.

tg.section: Red flag indicators related to anonymity; source of funds or wealth
tg.says: Funds to or from mixers, darknet markets, ransomware, fraud or theft addresses.

tg.section: Red flag indicators in the source of funds or wealth
tg.says: Transactions with addresses linked to sanctions or other illicit activity.
Screen counterparties and beneficiaries of incoming and outgoing crypto transfers; act on a hit.
Screening covers the transaction, not only the client; blockchain analysis before and after the transfer.

tg.section: Red flag indicators related to transactions
tg.says: Several high-value transfers in a short period, or staggered and then inactive.
Information on originator and beneficiary must accompany crypto-asset transfers between providers; missing information must be detected and handled.
Transfers to or from providers not authorised in the EU, decentralised platforms or self-hosted addresses are risk factors.
The report does not name peeling chains; its closest example is a chain of automated transfers across many wallets and exchanges.
Scams and fraud involving virtual assets keep rising.

gd.title: Virtual Assets Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing
gd.summary: Red flags drawn from more than 100 cases, grouped by transactions, transaction patterns, anonymity, senders or recipients, source of funds or wealth, and geography. A single indicator is not proof; several together without a business rationale raise suspicion.

gd.title: Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
gd.status: in force; does not reflect the 2025 revision of Recommendation 1
gd.summary: How the FATF Standards apply to virtual assets and VASPs: definitions, stablecoins, peer-to-peer transfers and unhosted wallets, licensing, the travel rule and counterparty due diligence.

gd.title: Seventh Targeted Update on Implementation of the FATF Standards on Virtual Assets/VASPs
gd.summary: Progress and gaps in implementing Recommendation 15; misuse of stablecoins by illicit actors, including DPRK actors and terrorist financiers, has kept increasing since the 2025 update.

gd.title: Travel Rule Guidelines (EBA/GL/2024/11): information requirements in relation to transfers of funds and certain crypto-assets transfers under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113
gd.summary: Which information must travel with a crypto-asset transfer, and the steps CASPs and intermediary CASPs take to detect missing or incomplete information and to handle such transfers.

gd.title: Guidelines amending the ML/TF Risk Factors Guidelines to cover crypto-asset service providers (EBA/GL/2024/01)
gd.summary: Sector-specific risk factors for CASPs, including the type of crypto-asset, products that hide the user's identity, and transfers to or from self-hosted addresses, decentralised platforms or providers not authorised in the EU.

gd.title: Sanctiescreening bij (inkomende en uitgaande) cryptotransacties
gd.summary: Crypto service providers screen counterparties and beneficiaries of incoming and outgoing transfers, not only their clients; measures are risk-based, acting on a hit is a strict obligation; unhosted wallets carry more risk; examples include blockchain analysis before and after the transfer and holding incoming crypto in an omnibus wallet until the counterparty is screened.

gd.title: Indicators that could point to unusual transactions in crypto service provision
gd.status: possibly withdrawn: a DNB overview of withdrawn Open Book statements lists this topic
gd.summary: Objective and subjective indicators for crypto services; a transaction profile per client; knowing the coins served, including contaminated coins. Points to FIU-NL for indicators.

queries.01_register:
// Who supervises crypto, in which role, under which laws? Per jurisdiction; wave 1 = the Netherlands.
// from: - | yields: Jurisdiction
MATCH (x:Jurisdiction)<-[:IN_JURISDICTION]-(s:Sector)<-[v:SUPERVISES]-(g:Regulator)
OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[:SUBJECT_TO]->(w:Law)
RETURN x.wave AS wave, x.code AS code, x.name AS jurisdiction, x.regime AS regime,
       collect(DISTINCT g.short + ' (' + v.role + ')') AS supervisors, collect(DISTINCT w.short) AS laws, x.verify AS verify
ORDER BY wave, jurisdiction
queries.02_cases:
// Every public crypto enforcement case: who, by whom, how much, which law, and the source. The Netherlands first, newest first.
// from: - | yields: Source
MATCH (k:Source {kind: 'case'})-[:IN_JURISDICTION]->(x:Jurisdiction)
OPTIONAL MATCH (k)-[:BY]->(g:Regulator)
OPTIONAL MATCH (k)-[:TYPOLOGY]->(ty:RiskCategory)
OPTIONAL MATCH (k)-[r:VIOLATED]->(w:Law)
RETURN x.code AS country, k.date AS date, k.party AS party, collect(DISTINCT g.short) AS authorities, k.measure AS measure,
       k.amount AS amount, k.currency AS currency, k.amount_note AS amount_note, collect(DISTINCT w.short + CASE WHEN r.art IS NULL OR r.art = '' THEN '' ELSE ' art. ' + r.art + CASE WHEN size(coalesce(r.lids, [])) > 0 THEN '(' + reduce(t = '', l IN r.lids | t + CASE t WHEN '' THEN '' ELSE ')(' END + l) + ')' ELSE '' END END) AS laws, collect(DISTINCT ty.name) AS typologies, k.status AS status, k.url AS source, k.decision AS decision, k.verify AS verify, k.id AS id
ORDER BY CASE x.code WHEN 'NL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, date DESC
queries.03_cases_by_law:
// Where did the same law go wrong before? Per law: the cases that violated it, and the total published amount per currency.
// from: - | yields: Law
MATCH (k:Source {kind: 'case'})-[:VIOLATED]->(w:Law)
WITH w, collect(DISTINCT k) AS ks
RETURN w.short AS law, w.title AS title, size(ks) AS cases, [k IN ks | k.party] AS parties,
       reduce(t = 0.0, k IN ks | t + CASE WHEN k.currency = 'USD' THEN coalesce(k.amount, 0.0) ELSE 0.0 END) AS usd,
       reduce(t = 0.0, k IN ks | t + CASE WHEN k.currency = 'EUR' THEN coalesce(k.amount, 0.0) ELSE 0.0 END) AS eur
ORDER BY cases DESC, law
queries.04_sanctions_lists:
// The sanctions lists a crypto screening checks against, who publishes them, and what the daily import found.
// from: - | yields: SanctionsList
MATCH (l:SanctionsList)
OPTIONAL MATCH (l)-[:PUBLISHED_BY]->(g:Regulator)
RETURN l.name AS list, g.short AS publisher, l.refresh AS refresh, l.imported AS imported, l.entries_total AS entries,
       l.addresses_total AS addresses, l.fetched AS fetched, l.url AS source
ORDER BY imported DESC, entries DESC, list
queries.06_same_party_elsewhere:
// The same company, sanctioned by more than one authority or in more than one country: where else did it go wrong?
// from: - | yields: Entity
MATCH (e:Entity)<-[:AGAINST]-(k:Source {kind: 'case'})-[:IN_JURISDICTION]->(x:Jurisdiction)
OPTIONAL MATCH (k)-[:BY]->(g:Regulator)
WITH e, k, x, collect(g.short) AS by
ORDER BY k.date
WITH e, collect(x.code + ' ' + k.date + ' ' + k.measure + ' (' + reduce(s = '', a IN by | s + CASE s WHEN '' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + a) + ')') AS cases, count(DISTINCT x) AS countries
WHERE size(cases) > 1
RETURN e.group AS group, e.name AS party, countries, cases
ORDER BY countries DESC, size(cases) DESC
queries.07_articles:
// Per article: the duty, how often it was violated in the cases (with the total of the fines in EUR, as published), and the article that replaced it.
// from: - | yields: Article
MATCH (x:Article)
OPTIONAL MATCH (k:Source {kind: 'case'})-[:VIOLATED_ARTICLE]->(x)
OPTIONAL MATCH (x)-[:REPLACED_BY]->(y:Article)
WITH x, y, collect(k) AS ks
RETURN x.law_short + ' art. ' + x.art AS article, x.heading AS heading, x.duty AS duty, x.status AS status, size(ks) AS cases,
       [k IN ks | k.party] AS parties,
       reduce(t = 0.0, k IN ks | t + CASE WHEN k.currency = 'EUR' AND k.measure ENDS WITH 'fine' THEN coalesce(k.amount, 0.0) ELSE 0.0 END) AS fines_eur,
       CASE WHEN y IS NULL THEN null ELSE y.law_short + ' art. ' + y.art END AS replaced_by
ORDER BY cases DESC, x.law_short, size(x.art), x.art
queries.08_exposure:
// Direct exposure on chain: the counterparties of a listed entity's addresses, what moved each way, and whether the
// counterparty is itself on a list. param: entity (e.g. OFAC:36025). Facts from the chain; who controls an unlisted address is not known.
// from: Entity | yields: Address
MATCH (e:Entity {id: $entity})-[:CONTROLS]->(a:Address)-[f:SENT]-(c:Address)
WHERE NOT (e)-[:CONTROLS]->(c)
WITH c, f, startNode(f) = a AS outgoing
OPTIONAL MATCH (x:Entity)-[:CONTROLS]->(c)
RETURN c.key AS counterparty, c.chain AS chain, f.asset AS asset,
       sum(CASE WHEN outgoing THEN f.amount ELSE 0.0 END) AS sent_to, sum(CASE WHEN outgoing THEN 0.0 ELSE f.amount END) AS received_from,
       sum(f.count) AS transfers, min(f.first) AS first, max(f.last) AS last, collect(DISTINCT x.name) AS listed_as
ORDER BY sent_to + received_from DESC
queries.10_typologies:
// The risk typology: per category its severity, how many listed entities and cases fall in it.
// from: - | yields: RiskCategory
MATCH (x:RiskCategory)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e:Entity)-[:IN_CATEGORY]->(x)
WITH x, count(DISTINCT e) AS entities
OPTIONAL MATCH (k:Source {kind: 'case'})-[:TYPOLOGY]->(x)
RETURN x.id AS id, x.name AS category, x.severity AS severity, x.group AS kind, x.description AS description, entities, count(DISTINCT k) AS cases
ORDER BY CASE x.severity WHEN 'severe' THEN 0 WHEN 'high' THEN 1 WHEN 'medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'low' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END, x.group, category
